ev.q: It is also a younger tradition than is commonly supposed.

1.why: B段首句是主旨，末句再次确认：同行评审是二战后才普及的。v A practice more recent than it appears ↔ a younger tradition than is commonly supposed。iv 是陷阱：爱因斯坦的论文并没有被拒，是他自己撤稿，而且只是段中一个例子。

ev.q: Whatever its origins, the process has clear limits.

2.why: C段讲审稿能查出什么、查不出什么：不看原始数据、不重复实验、BMJ 实验只发现约两处错误。ix What checking can and cannot catch ↔ the process has clear limits。vii 是细节陷阱：段中只顺带提到审稿人通常无报酬，没有主张付费；i 与原文相反，原文只说造假更难被发现，没说造假很普遍。

ev.q: argues that this kind of conservatism is built into the system

3.why: D段。viii Built-in caution towards the unfamiliar ↔ peer review may favour the familiar … this kind of conservatism is built into the system。

ev.q: The question is whether it can be supplemented.

4.why: E段先让步（不应废除同行评审），再讲预印本这种补充办法，最后讲它的风险（Ferreira）。iii Supplementing the system, with some dangers 涵盖了补充和风险两部分。x 过度推断：原文没有说匿名审稿会结束。

ev.q: regard peer review as the first stage of scrutiny rather than the last

5.why: F段。vi An early hurdle, not a final verdict ↔ the first stage of scrutiny rather than the last … passed a test; it does not tell us that the paper is true。

ev.q: To treat the label as a guarantee of truth is to ask of it something it cannot deliver.

6.why: A段。作者认为 this confidence rests on a misunderstanding，把这个标签当成真理保证是要求它做做不到的事。题干说记者这样做是对的，与作者观点相反。

ev.q: His indignation, it turned out, was misplaced: the referee had identified a genuine error

7.why: B段。had good reason to be angry ↔ 原文明确说 His indignation … was misplaced，因为审稿人确实发现了错误。

ev.q: They are usually unpaid and fit the work around their own research and teaching.

8.why: C段只陈述审稿人通常没有报酬，没有说付费会不会让他们做得更好。作者对此没有表态，所以是 NOT GIVEN。很多人会把 unpaid 和审稿漏错联系起来选 YES，这是推断，不是作者的说法。

ev.q: changed the authors' names and institutions to fictitious and obscure ones

9.why: D段。作者把这个研究当作 peer review may favour the familiar 的证据：同样的论文换成不知名的机构后几乎都被拒。Where a researcher works ↔ institutions。

ev.q: Authors themselves often report that reviewers' comments made their papers clearer and more careful

10.why: E段让步部分。improve the quality of papers ↔ made their papers clearer and more careful … filters out a great deal of weak work。作者在这里认可了同行评审的作用。

ev.q: deliberately inserted eight errors into a paper and sent it to several hundred reviewers; on average, each reviewer identified only about two of them

11.why: C段。planted mistakes ↔ deliberately inserted eight errors；only a small share ↔ only about two of them。C 与原文相反：most cases … are exposed after publication rather than before it。

ev.q: Most of the resubmissions went unrecognised, and almost all of those were rejected

12.why: D段。little-known places ↔ fictitious and obscure institutions；mostly rejected ↔ almost all of those were rejected。

ev.q: A reviewer who approves a mistaken paper risks embarrassment, she points out, whereas one who rejects an original but unusual idea suffers no penalty at all.

13.why: D段末句。the risks for a reviewer favour turning down new ideas ↔ approving a mistaken paper risks embarrassment, whereas rejecting an original idea suffers no penalty。

ev.q: unverified claims posted as preprints were widely reported in the press before anyone had checked them, sometimes with damaging consequences

14.why: E段末句。unchecked findings reach the media ↔ unverified claims … widely reported in the press；harm ↔ damaging consequences。A 是 Nature 的做法（B段）；F 是爱因斯坦的经历。
